concepts.label: User-Defined Functions (using UDFs in SQL++ statements)

relations.subject: js-udf:sql-managed-udf
relations.evidence: The following query creates a SQL++ managed JavaScript function in the current query context. ```sqlpp CREATE FUNCTION add100(num) LANGUAGE JAVASCRIPT AS "function add100(param1) {return param1+100;}"; ```

relations.subject: js-udf:external-function
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (requiresPriorExecutionOf) - creating a UDF that references a library requires the library and its JavaScript function to already exist
relations.evidence: If you have created a JavaScript function in a JavaScript library (see [Create a JavaScript Library](create-javascript-library.md)), you must create a SQL++ user-defined function to reference it.

relations.subject: js-udf:external-function
relations.evidence: The following query creates a user-defined function within the current query context that references a global JavaScript library. ```sqlpp CREATE FUNCTION GetBusinessDays(startDate, endDate) LANGUAGE JAVASCRIPT as "getBusinessDays" AT "my-library"; ```

relations.subject: js-udf:scoped-function
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - already established relation shape from round 6's javascript-functions-with-couchbase.json
relations.evidence: If required, [set the query context](select.md#query-context) for a scoped function, or unset the context for a global function.

relations.subject: js-udf:external-function
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (behavesDifferentlyUnder) - a scoped library forces a matching-scope UDF
relations.evidence: If the JavaScript library is scoped, create a scoped user-defined function in the same scope as the library.

relations.subject: n1ql:create-function
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted (usesEnum) - fixed-arity vs. variadic is a closed choice for how a UDF's parameter list is declared
relations.evidence: When you create a user-defined function, you can specify a list of parameters for any values you need to process or use in your function. If you want to create a user-defined function that can take a variable length list of parameters, you can create a **variadic** function.

notable_absence.finding: No role, privilege, or edition gate stated anywhere on this page for creating any of the three UDF types - each of the three creation tasks is given equal, parallel Query Tab + SQL++ tab treatment with no differentiating access requirement mentioned. This is consistent with round 6's finding that JS UDFs slot into the existing cluster read/write permission model rather than defining their own.

cross_component_finding: For each of the three UDF creation flavors (inline SQL++, SQL++-managed JavaScript, JavaScript-library-referencing), this guide gives a Query Tab UI procedure (Data Tools > Query > Functions section > Create (+) > Function > Function Name / access-level radio / Parameters field / Inline SQL++ or Inline JavaScript or UDF Library tab) side-by-side with the equivalent CREATE FUNCTION SQL++ syntax already documented in round 6/round 5's createfunction.json - a clean, non-duplicative mapping (UI steps new, SQL++ syntax reused verbatim) rather than an inconsistent re-description of the same CREATE FUNCTION reference content.
cross_product_finding: Not applicable - no SDK content; the JavaScript code sample from create-javascript-library.md (getBusinessDays) is reused as the running example across this page too ('CREATE FUNCTION GetBusinessDays(startDate, endDate) LANGUAGE JAVASCRIPT as "getBusinessDays" AT "my-library"'), confirming the three JS UDF guides in this batch (create-javascript-library, create-user-defined-function, call-user-defined-function) form one deliberately continuous worked example rather than three independent ones.
